padding over the cap: 8,193 bytes at maxTokens 1,024 (cap 8,192): DISCARD_OVERLONG

settings switch: INFER_ACCEPT.fileSha256 differs from the claim key: DISCARD_SETTINGS

settings switch: the engine commit differs from the claim row's

discard order: OVERLONG outranks CONCURRENT and SETTINGS
discard order: CONCURRENT outranks SETTINGS
a very fast peer: the ratio is capped at RATIO_CAP = 5,000
a zero elapsed time is treated as 1 ms (checked arithmetic)
tEnd is the LATER of INFER_END and the last chunk (a chunk after the end frame counts)
the claim's throttle onset is honoured by the prediction (onset 5,000 ms: coolMs at the decode rate, the rest at the steady rate)
5 kept observations of the half-speed peer: state DISCREPANT, and its placement is min(1000, median 500) = its true speed (prefill 50,000, decode 10,000)
4 kept observations are UNVERIFIED whatever the ratios (MIN_STATE = 5)
n = 0: prior' = claim x 700 / 1000 (prefill 70,000, decode 14,000)
n = 1: the blend (2 x prior' + claim x min(1000, x)) / 3
n = 2: the blend with two kept ratios
n = 3: the lower median of the kept ratios, capped at 1000
an even n takes the lower median x[(n - 1) / 2]: n = 6
an honest busy peer (queueing on 2 of 5): ratios {400, 450, 900, 950, 960}: best = x[3] = 950 -> CORROBORATED, placement min(1000, x[2] = 900)
a fast peer: every ratio above 1000 still places at the claim (effRatio = min(1000, median))
best = x[(3n)/4]: the upper quartile of 5 ratios is x[3]
truncation: four answers of < 128 bytes: the discard budget trips at the 4th, state WEAK, tracked rate clamped to the lowest ratio among observations of >= 8 bytes
truncation with every answer under 8 bytes: no qualifying observation, the tracked rate clamps to 0 (the candidate then fails F8)
exactly half discarded (2 of 4) does not trip the budget
more than half discarded (3 of 5) trips the budget even with kept ratios
the window keeps the last WIN = 20 kept ratios (25 observations)

the same padding against a peer only 7x slower: WEAK (the residual is bounded, not absent)
OVERLONG answers add a strike each and are never kept
a concurrent attempt is discarded and does not enter the window
state thresholds: best = 800 is CORROBORATED
state thresholds: best = 799 is WEAK
state thresholds: best = 600 is WEAK
state thresholds: best = 599 is DISCREPANT
the peer-wide 400 permille discount replaces 700 (n = 0: prefill 40,000)
capRef below the claim binds prior' while n < 3: min(claim, capRef) x 700 / 1000 (prefill 35,000)
capRef does not apply once n >= 3 (the observed median replaces the prior)
an inherited DISCREPANT state stays DISCREPANT whatever the new ratios say until it clears
ratios above 1000 in the window: the median is capped, the state uses the raw best
a WEAK budget clamp never lifts a lower tracked rate: min(median-based, minRatio-based)
the peer publishes a new claim seq twice in one day: the second is ignored for routing until 24 h pass
a claim body with a seq that is not higher is never accepted (rollback)

an inherited DISCREPANT state does not clear on 10 observations whose best is below CORR

a new claim seq 24 h later restarts W but not the discard budget: four truncated answers still read WEAK and still clamp the rate to the lowest ratio of an answer of >= 8 bytes (40 bytes: predicted 5,461 ms, ratio 27, prefill 2,700)
a new claim seq with every truncated answer under 8 bytes: the clamp is 0 and the candidate fails F8

a second penalty of a peer that is still DISCREPANT lasts 14 days (doubling on repeat)
a third penalty lasts 28 days
two files DISCREPANT only by inheritance (no observation, so no penalty was latched) still give disc 400
one file DISCREPANT by inheritance gives disc 700
two files DISCREPANT by ratios (best < 600) give disc 400
a running penalty gives disc 400 whatever the states are
a penalty that ended at now gives disc 700 when fewer than two files are DISCREPANT

R4-L-19 (a) trailing-whitespace padding: 1,200 letters then 600 newlines, 600 spaces and 600 tabs (3,000 raw bytes) in the honest time: normalised outBytes 1,200, ratio 973, exactly the unpadded answer (M08-002)
R4-L-19 (b) zero-width padding: 1,200 letters with 300 U+200B, 100 U+FEFF and 200 U+2060 (3 bytes each, 1,800 bytes of padding) interleaved: all Cf, removed: outBytes 1,200, ratio 973

R4-L-19 (c) a short real answer under a large max_tokens: 200 real letters then 32,568 spaces (32,768 raw bytes = the cap at max_tokens 4,096): normalised outBytes 200, outTokEst 50, predicted 7,461, elapsed 7,700: ratio 968, the honest ratio (invisible padding gains nothing)

R4-L-19 (c) the residual: the same 200 real letters then 32,568 VISIBLE filler letters (32,768 bytes = the cap) in the same time 7,700: outTokEst 8,192, E7 = 409,550, predicted 414,561, ratio capped at RATIO_CAP 5,000; the bound min(RATIO_CAP / 1000, 4,096 x 8 / 200) = min(5, 163.8) = 5 is reached; placement still cannot exceed the claim
R4-L-19: padding cannot rescue a short answer: 100 real letters then 1,000 newlines and 1,000 spaces: normalised outBytes 100 < SHORT_BYTES: DISCARD_SHORT
R4-L-19 NFC: 600 decomposed e + U+0301 (3 bytes each, 1,800 raw bytes) compose to 600 precomposed U+00E9 (2 bytes each): outBytes 1,200, ratio 973
R4-L-19 order: control characters are removed BEFORE whitespace runs collapse. 600 letters, a space, U+0007, a space, 599 letters: the two spaces meet and collapse to one: 600 + 1 + 599 = 1,200
R4-L-19 (ERR-R4B-TR-1): a newline is a control character and is removed, not collapsed to a space: 600 letters, a newline, 600 letters: outBytes 1,200 (not 1,201)

R4-L-19 whitespace: a run of mixed space separators (U+00A0, U+2003, U+2028, U+0020, U+3000) between two 600-letter halves collapses to ONE U+0020 (1 byte), a leading run and a trailing run (U+2029) are trimmed: outBytes 1,201

R4-L-19 chunk-split invariance: a whitespace run split across chunks, a zero-width character at a chunk edge and a decomposed e + U+0301 split across chunks give the same outBytes as one chunk: 400 letters + 1 + 400 letters + U+00E9 (2) + 397 letters = 1,200
R4-L-19 OVERLONG is judged on the normalised length: 8,192 letters (the cap at max_tokens 1,024) plus 5,000 U+200B (15,000 bytes of padding) are kept, outBytes 8,192

R4-L-18: one tracked ratio scales the claim decode AT P; it does not rescale the curve points first: ratios {900, 900, 900}, claim decode at P = 26,822: tracked decodeAtP = floor(26,822 x 900 / 1000) = 24,139 (scaling the points first would give 24,140); prefill 90,000, steady 18,000

R4-L-18: clamped below the curve: at P = 500 a curve whose first point is at 600 ((600, 30000)-(1024, 20000)) gives the first point, 30,000; n = 0: prior' = min(30,000, no capRef) x 700 / 1000 = 21,000

R4-L-18: a DISCREPANT window with NO claim body recorded before it (no earlier seq, no earlier acceptance), then the first claim body at 1,000 ms: it is accepted (nothing to wait 24 h for) and DISCREPANT is inherited until 10 good observations: 9 DISCREPANT then CORROBORATED

ERR-FX2-ASC01: five kept ratios of 500 (best 500 < 600: DISCREPANT) and six truncated answers (6 of 11 discarded: budget tripped): the budget never lifts DISCREPANT to WEAK; the clamp still applies: minRatio 5, tracked prefill 100,000 x 5 / 1000 = 500, decode 100, steady 100
ERR-FX2-ASC01 control: a tripped budget on a CORROBORATED window (best 900) turns it WEAK (the budget demotes)
ERR-FX2-ASC01 control: a tripped budget on an UNVERIFIED window (n = 4) is WEAK

ERR-FX2-ASC01: two files of one peer are each DISCREPANT (five ratios of 500) and then each truncates six answers (budget tripped): DISCREPANT is not lifted, so the penalty latches at the 5th kept observation of the second file (7 days from 2,000), is not extended by the later discards, and disc is 400 before, during and after it (both files are still DISCREPANT)

ERR-FX3-TP-1 variation-selector padding: 1,200 letters with 300 U+FE0F (3 bytes each) and 300 U+E0100 (4 bytes each, 2,100 bytes of padding) interleaved: both are default-ignorable (U+FE0F is Mn, U+E0100 is Mn), removed: outBytes 1,200, ratio 973, exactly the unpadded answer

ERR-FX3-TP-1 combining-grapheme-joiner and filler padding: 1,200 letters with 200 U+034F (Mn, 2 bytes), 100 U+115F (Lo, 3), 100 U+3164 (Lo, 3) and 100 U+FFA0 (Lo, 3) interleaved: all default-ignorable, removed: outBytes 1,200, ratio 973

ERR-FX3-TP-1 blank-glyph padding: 1,200 letters with 200 U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK (So, 3 bytes; not default-ignorable, listed by name), 100 U+17B4 (Mn) and 100 U+180B (Mn) interleaved: removed: outBytes 1,200, ratio 973

ERR-FX3-TP-2 NFC expansion is capped: 300 letters and 300 U+0958 (3 bytes each, 900 raw; NFC expands each to U+0915 U+093C, 6 bytes): the NFC form would be 2,100 bytes, more than was sent; outBytes is min(NFC form, the same text without NFC) = 1,200, ratio 973
ERR-FX3-TP-1 control: a visible combining mark is not invisible padding: 600 x (e + U+0300) is 1,800 raw bytes, NFC composes each pair to U+00E8 (2 bytes): outBytes 1,200, ratio 973

ERR-FX3-TP-4 a formatted honest answer on the NORMALISED basis: 133 indented lines and 4 letters (1,467 raw bytes, 1,200 after normalisation) in the honest time: outBytes 1,200, ratio 973, CORROBORATED-grade (>= 800) exactly like the plain 1,200-letter answer (M08-002); the bytes-per-token table is measured on this normalised text

ERR-FX3-TP-4 the trap, pinned: the same formatted answer from a lender running at 90 % of its claim when the table was (wrongly) measured on RAW bytes (4,000 bytes per token over 1,467 raw bytes = 367 tokens, honest time 23,311 / 0.9 = 25,901 ms): the tracker counts 1,200 normalised bytes (300 tokens, predicted 19,961), ratio floor(19,961,000 / 25,901) = 770 < 800: the tracker does not compensate, so a raw-basis table would mark honest formatted answers down; the table must be generated with AnswerText
RP-10 an unmeasured bandwidth (kbps 0, path LAN) takes the LAN default 100,000 kbit/s: E1 = 10 + ceilDiv(40,960, 100,000) = 11, exactly the worked numbers of M08-001: predicted 19,961 ms, ratio 973
